title: Why Trump’s Hail Mary on Fuel Prices Fell Short
gist: Johnson reports that Trump's pre-midterm efforts to lower fuel prices by buying Russian diesel and pressuring Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries have failed, with Brent above $117, U.S. gasoline at $4.20 and diesel at $6.32. Ukraine has resumed refinery strikes, Hormuz shipping now faces limpet mines, and the administration is reportedly weighing a post-midterm attack on Iran that Sen. Chris Murphy called 'insane.'

themes.theme: Fuel price surge from the Iran war

insights.claim: The global oil benchmark, about $70 a barrel before the Iran war began in February, rose to over $117 a barrel on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, and is climbing toward $120.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: A ~67% oil price rise is a major inflation and growth shock.
insights.quote: The global benchmark price of oil, which was about $70 a barrel before Trump started the Iran war in February, rose to over $117 a barrel on Friday.

insights.claim: U.S. average gasoline is $4.20 a gallon, more than a dollar above a year earlier, and no president has kept gasoline above $4 longer than Trump.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Consumer fuel costs are a direct midterm headwind and drag on discretionary spending.
insights.locator: The global benchmark price of oil

insights.claim: U.S. diesel at $6.32 a gallon is about 70% higher than a year ago, and diesel powers the entire economy.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Diesel spikes feed freight, agriculture and goods inflation; trucking and logistics margins under pressure.
insights.quote: Diesel, which powers the entire economy, is worse: At $6.32 a gallon, it is about 70 percent higher than one year ago.

insights.claim: Hormuz shipping faces high costs, Iranian drones and missiles, and for the first time limpet mines, keeping oil prices high.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Rising tanker insurance and freight costs sustain the oil risk premium.

insights.claim: Trump agreed in a call with Putin three weeks ago to buy Russian diesel, which is forbidden under U.S. law, but the three loaded Russian tankers may not be allowed to dock and U.S. traders fear sanctions exposure.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Sanctions-law conflicts block ad hoc supply fixes; don't count on Russian product easing U.S. diesel.

insights.so_what: Political supply gimmicks have negligible price impact against structural shortages.

themes.theme: Ukraine's refinery strikes and waning U.S. leverage

insights.claim: After pausing under U.S. pressure in October, Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil targets, including a devastating attack on a large Rosneft refinery that makes military jet fuel.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Renewed Russian refinery outages tighten global product markets, especially diesel and jet.

insights.claim: U.S. negotiators including Steve Witkoff said Kyiv should show 'gratitude' by curtailing strikes on Russian refineries.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Washington prioritizes domestic fuel prices over Ukraine's war aims.

insights.claim: U.S. leverage over Ukraine has shrunk because the Trump administration has delivered no new military or financial aid in its second term and has suspended some Starlink access and missile-strike intelligence sharing.
insights.speaker: Keith Johnson
insights.so_what: Ukraine will act independently on energy strikes, adding unpredictability to product markets.
